analyzed_vuln.description: `update_errors_warnings()` stores `*last_errors` into global `DATEG(last_errors)` when warnings/errors exist, but then unconditionally calls `timelib_error_container_dtor(*last_errors)` and nulls only the local pointer. This leaves `DATEG(last_errors)` dangling (pointing to freed memory). Later, during module post-deactivate (`zm_post_zend_deactivate_date`), `timelib_error_container_dtor(DATEG(last_errors))` is called again, causing a heap-use-after-free (read in `timelib_error_container_dtor` at timelib.c:159, then double-dtor behavior).
analyzed_vuln.conditions: PoV creates a `DateTime` with an invalid string (`"\xff"`), producing parse warnings/errors via `timelib_strtotime` in `php_date_initialize`. Data flow: harness executes PHP snippet -> `DateTime::__construct` -> `php_date_initialize` -> `update_errors_warnings(&err)`. If `err` has warning_count or error_count, `DATEG(last_errors)` is assigned the same container and then freed immediately. On request/module shutdown path (`zend_post_deactivate_modules` -> `zm_post_zend_deactivate_date`), the stale global is destructed again, triggering UAF.
